name: Ford Australia
overview: Ford Motor Company of Australia was established in Geelong, Victoria in March 1925 by Canadian-born Hubert French. Beginning with local assembly of the Model T in a disused wool store, Ford went on to become one of Australia's premier automotive manufacturers and innovators. In 1934, Ford Australia young designer Lewis Bandt invented the world's first coupe utility ('ute') in Geelong, creating an automotive category that defined rural and commercial Australia. In September 1960, Ford launched the Falcon, igniting a fierce 56-year rivalry with Holden. Operating major vehicle assembly and stamping complexes at Broadmeadows and engine and casting plants at Geelong, Ford designed, engineered, and manufactured iconic vehicles including the Falcon (XK through FG X), Fairlane, LTD, Territory SUV, and Capri convertible. Although local vehicle manufacturing ceased on 7 October 2016, Ford Australia transformed into Ford's Global Center of Excellence for Ranger and Everest, employing over 2,000 Australian engineers and designers at Campbellfield and the You Yangs Proving Ground.
australian_history:
Ford's Australian journey began on 31 March 1925 when Ford Motor Company of Canada established its Australian subsidiary in Geelong, Victoria. Construction of a state-of-the-art manufacturing plant began immediately alongside plants in Brisbane, Sydney, Adelaide, and Perth. In 1934, responding to a farmer's wife's letter requesting 'a vehicle to go to church in on a Sunday and carry the pigs to market on Monday', 24-year-old Geelong designer Lewis Bandt penned the 1934 Ford Coupe Utility, grafting a cargo tray behind a 2-door coupe cabin—thus creating the 'Aussie Ute'.

In 1959, Ford established its new headquarters and main assembly plant at Broadmeadows, Melbourne. Rejecting the British Zephyr, managing director Charles Smith championed the American compact Falcon for local production. Launched in September 1960 as the XK Falcon, it initially suffered from fragile front ball joints on unsealed outback roads. Ford responded with the 1965 XP Falcon Durability Run, running five stock Falcons continuously for 70,000 miles at an average 70 mph at You Yangs to demonstrate rugged Australian durability—winning the 1965 Wheels Car of the Year.

In 1967, Ford ignited the Australian muscle car era with the XR Falcon GT (Windsor 289ci V8), followed by the legendary XY Falcon GT-HO Phase III in 1971. Powered by a 351ci Cleveland V8 and producing around 380 bhp, the Phase III was the fastest four-door production car on earth and Allan Moffat took it to back-to-back Bathurst victories. In 1972, Ford debuted the XA Falcon—the first Falcon entirely designed and developed in Australia, featuring the famous 'Coke bottle' hardtop coupe.

Ford dominated the 1980s with the XD, XE, and XF Falcon series, introducing Watts-linkage coil rear suspension, alloy cylinder heads, and electronic fuel injection, making the XF the best-selling car in Australia. The 2002 BA Falcon brought the revolutionary 4.0L DOHC 24-valve 'Barra' inline-six and Control Blade independent rear suspension, while the 2004 SX Territory became the first and only Australian-designed and built SUV, winning the 2004 Wheels COTY. Facing declining large-car sales, rising manufacturing costs, and the high Australian dollar, Ford concluded 91 years of vehicle production on 7 October 2016 when the last blue FG X Falcon XR6 sedan rolled off the Broadmeadows line. Today, Ford Australia thrives as an engineering and development powerhouse, leading global development of the best-selling Ford Ranger and Everest.

models.name: Ford Falcon
models.overview: The Ford Falcon is one of the most storied names in Australian industrial and cultural history. Manufactured continuously at Broadmeadows, Victoria for 56 years (1960-2016) across seven distinct generations and over 3.5 million units, the Falcon fought an epic rivalry with the Holden Commodore. From the pioneering XK and the legendary XY GT-HO Phase III (the fastest 4-door production car in the world) to the Australian-designed XA hardtop, the bestselling XF, the indestructible Intech and Barra DOHC sixes, the high-revving Boss V8s, and the supercharged Sprint series, the Falcon embodied Australian engineering resilience and high performance.

models.name: Ford Cortina
models.overview: The Ford Cortina held a distinguished two-decade tenure in Australia, evolving from a nimble British compact into a uniquely Australian six-cylinder muscle sedan. Assembled locally from 1962 (Mk1 and Mk2), the Cortina achieved legendary status when the Bob Jane / Harry Firth Cortina GT500 won the 1965 Armstrong 500 at Mount Panorama, Bathurst. In 1971, Ford Australia undertook a daring local engineering feat with the TC and TD Cortina: modifying the British 'Coke-bottle' body with an elongated front structure to accommodate Ford Australia's heavy 200ci (3.3L) and 250ci (4.1L) Falcon inline-six engines. The European-styled TE (1977) and TF (1980) brought crisp lines, Ghia luxury, and the sporty X-Pack before being succeeded by the Mazda-based Telstar in 1982.

models.name: Ford F-Series (F-100 / F-250 / F-350 / F-150)
models.overview: The Ford F-Series is an enduring pillar of Australian outback, farming, and heavy towing history. Locally assembled in Australia across multiple decades in Victoria, New South Wales, and Queensland, Australian F-100s, F-250s, and F-350s were specifically tailored for harsh Aussie work, utilizing local 250ci Falcon straight-sixes, 300ci big sixes, and Geelong-cast 302ci and 351ci Cleveland V8s. In 2001, Ford Australia officially returned to the heavy-duty market with the mighty RN-series F-250 and F-350, powered by the thunderous 7.3L Navistar Power Stroke Turbo Diesel V8 (175 kW / 684 Nm), creating a cult legend among caravan haulers. In 2023, Ford Australia officially launched the Next-Gen F-150 in Australia, remanufactured to OEM right-hand drive in Mickleham, Victoria featuring the 298 kW 3.5L EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 and 4.5-tonne towing capacity.

models.name: Ford Mustang
models.overview: The Ford Mustang has a storied heritage in Australia stretching back six decades. In 1965, Ford Australia officially imported and converted 400 iconic 1965-1966 notchback Mustangs to right-hand drive at Homebush, NSW, while touring car legend Norm Beechey campaigned a 1965 Mustang to Australia's first Australian Touring Car Championship win for an American V8. In 2001, Ford Tickford Experience (FTE) in Campbellfield, Victoria undertook a heroic $4 million engineering program to convert 250 SVT Mustang Cobras featuring independent rear suspension and 240 kW 4.6L DOHC 32V modular V8s. In late 2015, Ford delivered the first global factory right-hand drive FM Mustang to Australia, creating unprecedented multi-year customer waiting lists. The FM/FN generations and all-new 2024+ S650 generation (featuring the 362 kW 5.0L Gen-4 Coyote V8 and 373 kW Dark Horse) made Mustang Australia's best-selling sports car for seven consecutive years.

models.name: Ford Territory
models.overview: The Ford Territory was the first and only sports utility vehicle (SUV) designed, engineered, and manufactured in Australia. Developed under the code-name 'E265' at a cost of $500 million, the Territory debuted in April 2004 and won the prestigious 2004 Wheels Car of the Year award. Available in 5- and 7-seat configurations, in rear-wheel drive and permanent all-wheel drive, the Territory combined car-like handling, Virtual Pivot Control front suspension, and generous interior packaging, spanning SX, SY, and SZ series with Barra I6, Barra Turbo, and 2.7L V6 turbo-diesel engines.

models.name: Ford Capri
models.overview: The Ford Capri represents two bold chapters of Australian automotive innovation. In May 1969, Ford Australia began assembling the sleek Mk1 Capri sports coupe at Homebush, NSW, offering the 1600cc Kent and the potent 3.0-litre 'Essex' V6 in the revered Capri GT 3000 (101 kW / 136 bhp), instantly creating an Australian street and track favorite. In 1989, Ford Australia embarked on Project SA30: designing and manufacturing a dedicated front-wheel-drive 2+2 roadster convertible in Campbellfield, Victoria. Styled by Ghia in Turin and utilizing Mazda 323 mechanicals, the Australian-built Capri (SA, SB, SC, SE) was exported in huge numbers to North America as the Mercury Capri. It produced the blistering turbocharged Capri XR2 and the rare Australian Tickford-tuned Capri Clubsprint Turbo.

models.name: Ford Escort
models.overview: The Ford Escort was Ford Australia's frontline small car and grassroots rally champion throughout the 1970s. Manufactured at Ford's Homebush plant in Sydney, the Australian Mk1 (1970-1975) featured the classic 'dogbone' front grille, Kent Crossflow engines (1.1L, 1.3L, and 1.6L GT), and the legendary imported Twin Cam and RS1600. In 1975, the Australian Mk2 debuted with a squarer aerodynamic profile. Ford Australia equipped the Mk2 with the lively 1.6L Kent and the potent 2.0L OHC Pinto engine, culminating in the iconic Escort RS2000 featuring a polyurethane droop-snoot front nose, four-spoke alloy wheels, Scheel sports bucket seats, and rally-bred handling.

models.name: Ford Laser
models.overview: The Ford Laser was one of Australia's most beloved small cars, dominating private sales and motoring awards across the 1980s and 1990s. Born from Ford's global partnership with Mazda (sharing the 323 platform), the Laser was manufactured at Ford's Homebush assembly plant in Sydney with distinct styling penned by Ford Australia's design studio. The Laser spawned the iconic 'TX3' badge—an Australian performance sensation that progressed from the twin-carb KA/KB Sport to the ferocious KC/KE and KF/KH TX3 Turbo 4WD, packing a 1.6L/1.8L turbocharged DOHC engine, full-time four-wheel drive, and digital instruments. Sourcing shifted to Japan in 1994 with the imported KJ, KL, and KQ series before the model was succeeded by the Focus.

models.name: Ford Fairlane & LTD
models.overview: The Ford Fairlane and LTD was Australia's definitive long-wheelbase luxury prestige sedan. Spanning four decades and eleven model series from the 1967 ZA to the 2007 BF Mk II, the Fairlane dominated Australian corporate, hire-car, and government limousine fleets. In 1973, Ford introduced the ultra-exclusive LTD (P5) riding on a limousine-class 121-inch wheelbase with concealed headlamps and standard 351 Cleveland V8. The Fairlane and LTD offered effortless V8 cruising, cavernous rear legroom, and refined Australian engineering.

models.name: Ford Focus
models.overview: The Ford Focus replaced the Laser in 2002 and immediately established itself as Australia's benchmark dynamic driver's car in the compact segment thanks to its revolutionary 'Control Blade' multi-link rear suspension. Across four generations (LR, LT/LV, LW/LZ, and SA), the Focus earned critical acclaim. For Australian car enthusiasts, the Focus name was cemented by legendary performance flagships: the 2.0L high-revving LR ST170 (127 kW), the five-cylinder turbo LT/LV XR5 Turbo (166 kW 2.5L Volvo turbo) and limited-edition 224 kW Focus RS, the sensational 257 kW drift-mode AWD LZ Focus RS, and the nimble SA Focus ST.

models.name: Ford Ranger
models.overview: The Ford Ranger is Australia's best-selling vehicle and one of the country's crowning engineering triumphs. Designed, engineered, and developed from the ground up by Ford Australia's 2,000-strong engineering and design team at Campbellfield, Victoria and the You Yangs Proving Ground, the Ranger is exported to over 180 countries. Across the PJ/PK, the revolutionary T6 (PX I, II, III), and the Next-Gen (PY), the Ranger redefined dual-cab refinement, off-road ability, and high-speed off-road performance through the bespoke Ranger Raptor.

models.name: Ford Everest
models.overview: While built at AutoAlliance Thailand in Rayong, the Ford Everest was conceived, designed, engineered, and durability-tested in Australia by Ford's 2,000-strong global product development hub at Campbellfield and the You Yangs Proving Ground. Developed concurrently with the Ranger ute, the Everest transformed the T6 ladder-frame architecture into a refined 7-seat family wagon featuring coil-sprung Watt's linkage rear suspension, electronic terrain management, and 3.1-tonne towing. The 2015 UA series launched with the rugged 3.2L 5-cylinder Duratorq turbo-diesel and later 2.0L Bi-Turbo with 10-speed auto. The 2022+ UB Next-Gen Everest elevated the platform into an opulent, class-leading 4WD with standard 3.5-tonne towing and a flagship 3.0L V6 Turbo Diesel producing 184 kW and 600 Nm.

f-series.overview: The Ford F-Series is an enduring pillar of Australian outback, farming, and heavy towing history. Locally assembled in Australia across multiple decades in Victoria, New South Wales, and Queensland, Australian F-100s, F-250s, and F-350s were specifically tailored for harsh Aussie work, utilizing local 250ci Falcon straight-sixes, 300ci big sixes, and Geelong-cast 302ci and 351ci Cleveland V8s. In 2001, Ford Australia officially returned to the heavy-duty market with the mighty RN-series F-250 and F-350, powered by the thunderous 7.3L Navistar Power Stroke Turbo Diesel V8 (175 kW / 684 Nm), creating a cult legend among caravan haulers. In 2023, Ford Australia officially launched the Next-Gen F-150 in Australia, remanufactured to OEM right-hand drive in Mickleham, Victoria featuring the 298 kW 3.5L EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 and 4.5-tonne towing capacity.
f-series.australian_market_notes: Australian-assembled F-100s and F-250s featured unique 'Ambulance' high-output alternators, dual fuel tanks, heavy-duty Dana axles, and Australian-built Cleveland V8 engines manufactured at Geelong. The 2001-2007 RN F-250 with the 7.3L Power Stroke V8 became an instant legend, with second-hand examples frequently selling for higher than their original retail prices two decades later.

mustang.overview: The Ford Mustang has a storied heritage in Australia stretching back six decades. In 1965, Ford Australia officially imported and converted 400 iconic 1965-1966 notchback Mustangs to right-hand drive at Homebush, NSW, while touring car legend Norm Beechey campaigned a 1965 Mustang to Australia's first Australian Touring Car Championship win for an American V8. In 2001, Ford Tickford Experience (FTE) in Campbellfield, Victoria undertook a heroic $4 million engineering program to convert 250 SVT Mustang Cobras featuring independent rear suspension and 240 kW 4.6L DOHC 32V modular V8s. In late 2015, Ford delivered the first global factory right-hand drive FM Mustang to Australia, creating unprecedented multi-year customer waiting lists. The FM/FN generations and all-new 2024+ S650 generation (featuring the 362 kW 5.0L Gen-4 Coyote V8 and 373 kW Dark Horse) made Mustang Australia's best-selling sports car for seven consecutive years.
mustang.australian_market_notes: The 2001 Tickford Cobra conversion was a monumental engineering triumph: TVE completely re-engineered the front floor pan, steering rack, wiring harness, and air conditioning to OEM right-hand drive standards, winning full compliance approval under Australian Design Rules. In modern times, the Mustang represents Ford Australia's primary weapon in Supercars Championship touring car racing, carrying the blue oval flag across Mount Panorama.

territory.name: Ford Territory
territory.overview: The Ford Territory was the first and only sports utility vehicle (SUV) designed, engineered, and manufactured in Australia. Developed under the code-name 'E265' at a cost of $500 million, the Territory debuted in April 2004 and won the prestigious 2004 Wheels Car of the Year award. Available in 5- and 7-seat configurations, in rear-wheel drive and permanent all-wheel drive, the Territory combined car-like handling, Virtual Pivot Control front suspension, and generous interior packaging, spanning SX, SY, and SZ series with Barra I6, Barra Turbo, and 2.7L V6 turbo-diesel engines.
territory.australian_market_notes: Conceived under Ford Australia president Geoff Polites as Australian families began migrating from traditional large station wagons to high-riding SUVs, the Territory was engineered specifically for Australian family road trips, outback gravel touring, and boat towing. It featured 30 interior storage compartments, an independently opening tailgate glass window, and standard electronic stability control (ESC)—the first Australian-built car with standard ESC. Over 178,000 Territory SUVs were manufactured at Broadmeadows before local production concluded in October 2016.

capri.overview: The Ford Capri represents two bold chapters of Australian automotive innovation. In May 1969, Ford Australia began assembling the sleek Mk1 Capri sports coupe at Homebush, NSW, offering the 1600cc Kent and the potent 3.0-litre 'Essex' V6 in the revered Capri GT 3000 (101 kW / 136 bhp), instantly creating an Australian street and track favorite. In 1989, Ford Australia embarked on Project SA30: designing and manufacturing a dedicated front-wheel-drive 2+2 roadster convertible in Campbellfield, Victoria. Styled by Ghia in Turin and utilizing Mazda 323 mechanicals, the Australian-built Capri (SA, SB, SC, SE) was exported in huge numbers to North America as the Mercury Capri. It produced the blistering turbocharged Capri XR2 and the rare Australian Tickford-tuned Capri Clubsprint Turbo.
capri.australian_market_notes: The Australian-built SA-SE convertible was a landmark manufacturing achievement for Ford Australia, generating vital export income ($1 billion+) with over 66,000 built. The limited-production Capri Clubsprint by Tickford Vehicle Engineering (TVE) featured aggressive front air dams, high-flow turbocharger boosting to 105 kW, Momo steering wheel, and bespoke Australian-tuned sports suspension.

escort.name: Ford Escort
escort.overview: The Ford Escort was Ford Australia's frontline small car and grassroots rally champion throughout the 1970s. Manufactured at Ford's Homebush plant in Sydney, the Australian Mk1 (1970-1975) featured the classic 'dogbone' front grille, Kent Crossflow engines (1.1L, 1.3L, and 1.6L GT), and the legendary imported Twin Cam and RS1600. In 1975, the Australian Mk2 debuted with a squarer aerodynamic profile. Ford Australia equipped the Mk2 with the lively 1.6L Kent and the potent 2.0L OHC Pinto engine, culminating in the iconic Escort RS2000 featuring a polyurethane droop-snoot front nose, four-spoke alloy wheels, Scheel sports bucket seats, and rally-bred handling.
escort.australian_market_notes: Australian Escorts featured unique local content including Australian-made glass, batteries, interior trim, and heavy-duty front suspension struts tailored to corrugated rural backroads. The Escort RS2000 was an instant youth idol, while the Escort Sundowner panel van tapped into the 1970s surf van craze with bold bodyside sunset decals and rear bubble port-hole windows.

laser.australian_market_notes: The Laser was the best-selling small car in Australia throughout the 1980s, repeatedly outselling the Toyota Corolla and Holden Gemini. fairlane-ltd.name: Ford Fairlane & LTD
fairlane-ltd.overview: The Ford Fairlane and LTD was Australia's definitive long-wheelbase luxury prestige sedan. Spanning four decades and eleven model series from the 1967 ZA to the 2007 BF Mk II, the Fairlane dominated Australian corporate, hire-car, and government limousine fleets. In 1973, Ford introduced the ultra-exclusive LTD (P5) riding on a limousine-class 121-inch wheelbase with concealed headlamps and standard 351 Cleveland V8. The Fairlane and LTD offered effortless V8 cruising, cavernous rear legroom, and refined Australian engineering.
fairlane-ltd.australian_market_notes: Engineered by stretching the Falcon's wheelbase behind the B-pillar, the 1967 ZA Fairlane was a brilliant marketing stroke, completely outselling Holden's imported and adapted prestige offerings and prompting Holden to hurriedly develop the Brougham and Statesman. In 1973, the Australian LTD was born as the most expensive and luxurious domestic car in Australia. The line transitioned through modern alloy-head EFI sixes in the 1980s, the return of Windsor V8 power in the 1990s, Tickford performance editions, and the 5.4L 3-valve V8 in the final BA/BF series.

For Australian car enthusiasts, the Focus name was cemented by legendary performance flagships: the 2.0L high-revving LR ST170 (127 kW), the five-cylinder turbo LT/LV XR5 Turbo (166 kW 2.5L Volvo turbo) and limited-edition 224 kW Focus RS, the sensational 257 kW drift-mode AWD LZ Focus RS, and the nimble SA Focus ST.

In 2016, the LZ Focus RS created a national sensation when all 500 Australian allocation units sold out in days, driven by its 257 kW twin-scroll turbo engine and headline-grabbing 'Drift Mode' all-wheel drive.

ranger.name: Ford Ranger
ranger.overview: The Ford Ranger is Australia's best-selling vehicle and one of the country's crowning engineering triumphs. Designed, engineered, and developed from the ground up by Ford Australia's 2,000-strong engineering and design team at Campbellfield, Victoria and the You Yangs Proving Ground, the Ranger is exported to over 180 countries. Across the PJ/PK, the revolutionary T6 (PX I, II, III), and the Next-Gen (PY), the Ranger redefined dual-cab refinement, off-road ability, and high-speed off-road performance through the bespoke Ranger Raptor.
ranger.australian_market_notes: In 2006, Ford replaced the Courier with the PJ Ranger. In 2011, Ford Australia unveiled 'Project T6' (PX Ranger)—the first vehicle developed from a clean sheet in Australia for global Ford truck production. It introduced the rugged 3.2L 5-cylinder Duratorq diesel, 3.5-tonne towing, and 800mm water wading. In 2018, Ford Australia launched the Ranger Raptor featuring Fox Racing 2.5-inch Internal Bypass dampers and coil-sprung Watts-link rear suspension. In 2022, the Next-Gen (PY) Ranger debuted with a 3.0L V6 Turbo Diesel (184kW/600Nm) and the Raptor packing a twin-turbo 3.0L EcoBoost V6 producing 292kW, becoming Australia's #1 selling motor vehicle overall.

everest.overview: While built at AutoAlliance Thailand in Rayong, the Ford Everest was conceived, designed, engineered, and durability-tested in Australia by Ford's 2,000-strong global product development hub at Campbellfield and the You Yangs Proving Ground. Developed concurrently with the Ranger ute, the Everest transformed the T6 ladder-frame architecture into a refined 7-seat family wagon featuring coil-sprung Watt's linkage rear suspension, electronic terrain management, and 3.1-tonne towing. The 2015 UA series launched with the rugged 3.2L 5-cylinder Duratorq turbo-diesel and later 2.0L Bi-Turbo with 10-speed auto. The 2022+ UB Next-Gen Everest elevated the platform into an opulent, class-leading 4WD with standard 3.5-tonne towing and a flagship 3.0L V6 Turbo Diesel producing 184 kW and 600 Nm.
everest.australian_market_notes: The Everest effectively succeeded the Australian-built Ford Territory as Ford's family SUV champion, adding genuine outback off-road capability (800mm water wading) that the car-based Territory could never match. Australian suspension engineers spent thousands of hours tuning the Watt's linkage rear axle on Australian gravel, dirt, and corrugations to achieve an unprecedented blend of highway ride isolation and cornering grip.
